# locobench-claude-5-test

**14 families, 70 items**, generated by `claude-opus-5` through the IBM LiteLLM gateway and
validated by a 3-model cross-vendor committee (`gpt-5.6-terra`, `gemini-3.1-pro`,
`claude-sonnet-5`; V1 any-of, V3/V4 majority).

The corpus spans **all four ladder types**, **14 of the 36 canonical topics** and **all four
domains**. Family ids are **contiguous, f001-f014**:

| family | ladder | topic | domain |
|---|---|---|---|
| f001 | CONFLICT | Anthropology | Social Sciences |
| f002 | CONFLICT | Archaeology | Humanities |
| f003 | CONTROL | Art | Humanities |
| f004 | ORDER | Artificial Intelligence | Engineering & Technology |
| f005 | CHAIN | Astronomy | Natural Sciences |
| f006 | CONFLICT | Biology | Natural Sciences |
| f007 | ORDER | Botany | Natural Sciences |
| f008 | CONFLICT | Chemistry | Natural Sciences |
| f009 | CHAIN | Civil Engineering | Engineering & Technology |
| f010 | CONFLICT | Computer Science | Engineering & Technology |
| f011 | ORDER | Culture | Humanities |
| f012 | CONFLICT | Cybersecurity | Engineering & Technology |
| f013 | CONFLICT | Economics | Social Sciences |
| f014 | CONFLICT | Education | Social Sciences |

Ladder mix: 8 CONFLICT, 3 ORDER, 2 CHAIN, 1 CONTROL.

670 gold edges, validity split 0.61 valid (target 0.55), and every no-prior-gold sense is
represented: `Instantiation` 38, `Restatement` 93, `Contrast` 90, `Concession` 74,
`Alternative` 78, `Disjunction` 70. `Instantiation` was absent from the original 2-family
corpus entirely.

**All 202 ordering constraints across the 14 families are achievable** (no family carries a
constraint that is unsatisfiable by construction), all 14 pass the per-rung adjacency gate,
and every family carries 5 distinct response texts -- except f003, whose CONTROL ladder is
symmetric by design (rungs 0/4 both `ordering_only`, 1/3 both `direction_reversal`, so 3
distinct texts is its correct signature).

## Regenerating

The dataset name is kept at `locobench-claude-5-fixed` so item ids stay stable and keep
matching the published results in `results/locobench_claude_5_*`. The directory was renamed
from `locobench-claude-5-fixed` to `-test`; `config.json`'s `dataset_name` and the item ids
still carry the old name deliberately — they record what generated the items.

```sh
set -a && . ./.env && set +a
export OPENAI_API_KEY="$ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"   # the IBM LiteLLM gateway token

# fr2 has mellea_ibm; .venv does not. Not installed as a console script there, so -m.
# Generation is SEQUENTIAL (max_concurrency is not consumed) at ~45 s/call, so run it
# detached -- a single family exceeds a 10-minute foreground timeout.
nohup /path/to/envs/fr2/bin/python -u -m fact_reasoner.locobench.cli \
    --config configs/locobench_claude.json \
    --out data/locobench-claude-5-test \
    --dataset-name locobench-claude-5-fixed \
    --n-families 16 --limit 16 > /tmp/locobench.log 2>&1 &
```

`--n-families 16 --limit 14` targets exactly f001-f014; the two spare slots exist because
reaching a contiguous 14 took more attempts than slots. Re-running
the same command resumes — admitted families are skipped, so a completed run costs nothing.
Check the printed `validation panel ... (3 rater(s))` line before trusting a run; a panel that
degrades to one rater lets a single model decide admission.

## Three generator bugs this corpus exposed and fixed

**1. The ORDER ladder's three shuffle rungs were identical.** `shuffle_full`,
`shuffle_block` and `shuffle_adjacent` all rendered as `shuffle_order(r000)` — an edge id
where the P5 prompt documents `shuffle_order(level)` — so the model returned byte-identical
prose three times and the ladder's strict-increase constraints over pairs (0,1) and (1,2)
became unsatisfiable. Measured ceiling 9/15 on the first ORDER family. Fixed by
`perturb.SHUFFLE_LEVELS`, which maps the rung name to its level. f004 was regenerated;
f007 and f011 were generated fresh with the fix. All three now carry 5 distinct responses
with the edge set correctly invariant.

**2. CONFLICT plans lacked droppable conflict edges.** A CONFLICT ladder's deepest rung
applies `add_resolution` plus two *distinct* `drop_relation` calls, and only conflict-coupled
edges are eligible for either. Only three senses compile to a conflict coupling
(`Alternative`→exclusive, `Concession`/`Contrast`→contradiction), so P3 instruction 5's
one-of-each mandate yielded exactly three — and when the Concession was marked resolved, only
two were droppable and rung 4 collapsed onto rung 3. The worked example in instruction 10
carried exactly that failing shape, teaching it. Fixed in three places: instruction 5 now
demands ≥4 conflict-sensed relations with ≤1 resolved, the worked example was corrected to
satisfy it, and — because prose alone did not work — `parse.parse_plan` now *enforces* it, so
the complaint reaches the sampling loop and the plan is repaired in the same call instead of
failing after the whole respond stage has been paid for.

**3. A perturbation could return the prose unchanged.** `add_resolution` set the resolution
flag on f013's gold edge but handed back the base response verbatim, so rungs 1 and 2 shipped
identical text with differing labels. The adjacency gate passed it legitimately -- that gate
compares edge SIGNATURES, and those did differ -- leaving a `c1` strict-increase assertion
that a gold-arm readout can satisfy and a mined arm never can (corpus ceiling 201/202). Fixed
by `validate.gate_text_changed`, checked per call in the P5 loop against the text that call
was handed, so a composed rung whose *second* call no-ops is caught too. It is
whitespace-insensitive, and unlike the adjacency gate it has **no exemption list**:
`shuffle_order` and `ordering_only` are factor-invariant but both still rewrite prose, so a
text-side exemption would silently readmit this defect. Note this also required a `mock.py`
fix -- its fixed-string replacements made composed rungs no-op offline, which would have made
the dry-run reject ladders the live pipeline admits.

## Rejections

`rejected/` is **empty**: every family that was rejected during construction was subsequently
regenerated and admitted. The gate verdicts that shaped the corpus are recorded here instead,
since they are evidence about the prompts rather than noise:

| family | rejected at | cause | resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| f006 Biology | `V3.spans` | **unanimous 3/3 leakage** -- the prose used the word "disjunction", a relation-sense name. A true positive: P4 must not let a reader detect that a plan exists. | regenerated; new prose carries no sense-name leak |
| f006, f009, f012, f013 | `P5.rung4.edge_effect` | droppable conflict edges = 2, so rung 4's second `drop_relation` was a no-op and its edge set collapsed onto rung 3's | fixed by bug 2 above; all four then admitted on their first fresh plan |
| f013 Economics | *(passed all gates)* | `add_resolution` left the prose unchanged -- caught only by post-hoc analysis, not by any gate | fixed by bug 3 above; regenerated with 5 distinct texts |

Two things learned the hard way while diagnosing these:

* **A retry replays the stored plan.** `generate_family` reuses `artifacts["plan"]` verbatim
  (its docstring: *"a family with a validated plan does not re-plan"*), so a family rejected
  for a plan-level defect fails identically on every attempt and a plan-stage fix cannot reach
  it. To make one re-plan, delete `artifacts.plan` (and `response`) from its `state.json`
  entry. This is why f006, f009, f012 and f013 each burned attempts to no effect before the
  plans were cleared.
* **Generation is strictly sequential** -- `max_concurrency` is set but not consumed -- at
  roughly 45 s/call, so a single family exceeds a 10-minute foreground timeout. Run detached.

## Evaluation

The LCS evaluations in `results/locobench_claude_5_*` were produced against the **2-family**
version of this corpus and have not been re-run against these 14 families. See those
directories' own notes for the arms and caveats (notably: `windowed` is forward-only, and
`all_pairs` visits each unordered pair twice without dedup, so a policy comparison is not a
clean coverage ablation).
